summary: This schedule explains how a company must handle shares that are unclaimed by their owners. It covers sending reminders, moving unclaimed shares into special suspense accounts, and giving them back when the rightful owner asks. It also tells the company how to handle corporate benefits and voting rights for these shares.
points: The listed entity may give the procedural tasks to a registrar to an issue and share transfer agent.
The listed entity must send at least three reminders to the addresses available for both physical and demat shares.
Unclaimed demat shares must be moved to a demat suspense account, and physical shares must be moved to a single folio and dematerialised.
The company must keep records of each individual allottee whose shares are in these suspense accounts.
Voting rights on these unclaimed shares must stay frozen until the owner claims them.
example: Aarav Industries Limited noticed that some shareholders did not claim their shares after an issue. To follow the rules, the company sent three reminders to the addresses found in their records and application forms. Since the owners did not reply, Aarav Industries Limited moved the unclaimed demat shares into a special demat suspense account and dematerialised the physical shares into an unclaimed suspense account. They carefully kept the details of every allottee. Months later, a shareholder named Rohan approached the company to claim his shares. After proper verification of Rohan's identity, Aarav Industries Limited transferred the shares directly to Rohan's demat account, successfully completing the return of his rightful entitlement.

watch: People often confuse keeping these shares in a suspense account as the company taking ownership, but the company holds them purely on behalf of the rightful owners.
